absent: Full layouts of host CPU context, boot argument records, init parameter blocks, host MMU, pools, page descriptors and page table operation vectors beyond the fields and uses shown.
Numeric values and encodings for power state function identifiers, return codes, power states, hardware masks, CPU sentinel values, protection attributes, table flags and ownership identifiers.
Contracts of firmware forwarding and invocation helpers, logical map lookup, memory range lookup, component locking, fault info extraction and address translation helpers not in scope.
Hypervisor entry and resume entry register state, per CPU storage layout and lifetime, and release protocol details for successful CPU turn on beyond the stated handoff.
Exception syndrome, program status, control register and fault register field layouts and the full vector and trapping architecture beyond the observed synthesis and repaint rules.
Host hypercall, secure monitor call and abort handler internals, tracing payloads, and capability detection semantics behind the observed gates.
Stage two table mechanics including granule sizes, level handling, leaf validity and permission checks, forced entry callback, virtualization control derivation and memblock image layout.
Temporary mapping slot implementation, cache maintenance primitives, list poison values and allocator failure and concurrency behaviour beyond the shown checks.
Exact fault address decoding, non secure marking requirements and host abort handler expectations for the injected marker bit.

findings.text: Host CPU power on relay validates the requested affinity and rejects targets outside the initialized set. It ensures a single concurrent boot attempt per target through a dedicated boot record, records the requested resume address and argument with ordering, then forwards to firmware with hypervisor entry and per target init data. The record stays held on success for release by the arriving CPU and is released locally on firmware failure.

Target lookup first discards identifiers with bits outside the hardware mask, then scans the logical map for an exact match and returns a sentinel when none matches. This confines bootable targets to CPUs present at initialization time.

Boot coordination uses an atomic acquire transition from unlocked to locked for turn on, with a release store to unlock. Self suspend paths use a separate per CPU record and need no acquisition because only the running core writes its own record while concurrent turn on traffic uses a different record.

The legacy power state dispatcher forwards informational and migration related requests plus shutdown and reset directly, routes suspend and turn on to dedicated relay helpers that substitute hypervisor resume state, and reports unsupported for anything else. The newer dispatcher forwards feature and mode controls plus newer shutdown variants, routes system suspend to its helper, and delegates all remaining identifiers to the legacy dispatcher.

Both self suspend helpers stash the caller provided resume address and argument into the current core suspend record and invoke firmware with hypervisor resume entry and init data. Shallow states return to the caller while deep states re enter through the resume entry, and system suspend is specified to return only on error.

Top level host trap entry reads the trapped syndrome and dispatches hypercalls, secure monitor calls, lower level aborts and trapped system register accesses to dedicated handlers, applying a memory tagging filter first for system traps. Any other class is fatal, and entry and exit tracing brackets the handling.

Host exception synthesis selects the vector offset from the saved status mode, preserves a small set of condition and control flags into a new handler status with debug and interrupt masks set, adjusts privilege and tagging controls from host registers and capability checks, copies fault address only for translation faults, then installs the supplied syndrome plus saved return state for host entry.

Trapped accesses to the tag checking register group are treated as tagging faults only when the corresponding hypervisor trap controls indicate tagging is the cause. Mismatched controls fall through to fatal handling, while genuine cases are converted into a host undefined instruction fault and reported as handled.

Host stage two fault entry attempts to resolve fault info and silently retries when resolution fails due to concurrent table change. It requires the fault to be marked non secure, decodes the fault address from the hypervisor fault register, then drives demand mapping where permission conflicts inject a host abort while already mapped and success are benign and any other result is fatal.

Demand mapping classifies the fault address as regular memory or device input output via a range lookup to select protection attributes, then under the host component lock adjusts the target range to a mappable granule and performs the locked identity map.

Range adjustment requires the host lock and looks up the leaf entry for the fault address. It reports already present as existence and already poisoned entries as permission failure with an added consistency check for memory pages, otherwise promotes the request to the largest supported block mapping contained in the supplied range.

A memory interval is represented as a half open pair of 64 bit bounds with start inclusive and end exclusive. Containment holds when the parent start is at or below the child start and the child end is at or below the parent end.

Abort reinjection repaints lower level abort classes to current level equivalents when the trapped context was privileged. It marks the syndrome with the walk indicator bit reserved at host level to distinguish hypervisor injected faults, then delivers it through host exception synthesis.
Host stage two table creation combines the treat as stage one and identity map attribute flags.
Donation encodings reserve a low owner field spanning bits one through three and an extra field spanning bits four through fifty nine for additional donation state.
Guest ownership encodings reserve bits zero through fifteen for the owner handle and bits sixteen through fifty five for the guest frame number.

Host protection state centers on a global host MMU object plus a dedicated page table pool and a per CPU pointer to the current protected virtual machine with a shorthand accessor for the current entry.

Host mapping and pool mutation are serialized by a host component lock asserted by range adjustment and held across adjust plus map, by a pool lock held across page reference count changes, and by a large mapping lock held while a big temporary mapping slot is occupied.

The logical to hardware map defaults every slot to an invalid hardware identifier and is write protected after init. The hypervisor per CPU base array plus an offset helper derive each CPU area as the difference between its registered base and the per CPU section start after bounds validation.

List mutation validators verify neighbor linkage consistency and reject poisoned or self referential insertions and deletions. They report corruption through a common helper that faults or warns depending on build configuration and return a boolean verdict.

Splitting a compound hypervisor page resets the head order and marks each tail as an independent reference counted order zero page. Reference acquisition and release translate addresses to page descriptors and adjust counts under the owning pool lock.

Host stage two setup establishes virtualization controls from hardware capability registers, initializes the host lock, creates the dedicated pool and operation vector, builds the stage two tables with a forced entry callback, then publishes the root physical address and zeroes the virtual machine identifier.

Host and guest stage two allocators provide exact size zeroed concatenations that must match the rounded order size and split compound results, single page zeroed allocations with a memcache fallback for guests that clears and initializes the reference count, and paired reference acquisition and release against the owning pool.

Guest data and instruction cache maintenance are skipped when hardware coherency or invalidation capabilities make them unnecessary. Otherwise an address range walker aligns the interval to page boundaries and applies the requested operation chunk by chunk through large block or single page temporary mappings.

Device cleanup unmaps every gap between recorded memory regions plus the tail up to the table input size. Hypervisor text detection checks containment in the page rounded text image translated to physical, and early identity mapping treats already mapped as success because permissions never change after init.
A host entry is classified as hypervisor owned only when it is invalid and carries the donation invalid type and its owner field decodes to the hypervisor identifier.

Unexpected states escalate to fatal or warning diagnostics. These include unknown trap classes, unresolved fault addresses or unexpected mapper results, invalid granule promotion, mismatched allocation sizes, failed detached table walks, non singular table reference counts and inconsistent host page states.

Temporary mapping helpers expose a large block mapping attempt that degrades to single page mapping when the large window is unavailable, with a paired unmap that clears the slot and releases the associated lock when present.

Detached stage two table teardown walks the removed table over a zero based range sized by the table level with leaf and post table callbacks. It requires the walk to succeed and the table reference count to be singular, then releases the table.
Query helpers expose per CPU offset derivation with bounds enforcement, hypervisor text containment testing and hypervisor ownership testing for host entries for use by protection and fault paths.
